A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ConDA work and retain matching methods, datasets, and benchmark results. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation, prediction, classification, and representation-analysis results across five domains, including the experiments in Tables 1–2, Figures 3–5, and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds forecasting, inversion-solver, decoder, and neural-activity evaluations, including Tables 2 and 8–11 and the expanded Figure 5.

M1.justification: v2 adds ConDA implementations using Rex-RK4 inversion/sampling and IsoDiff latents alongside the original DDIM/cLDM pipeline. These extend the available inference procedures, while the contrastive objective, spline/TEX/KDE traversal, and core kNN lifting approach remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use fluid flow, calcium imaging, DISFA, TMS E-fields, and monkey-reaching spiking data. Generation, interpolation, held-out prediction, classification, class transfer, and interpretability remain the task coverage; the added horizons, solvers, and decoder configurations extend evaluation within that coverage.

E2.justification: v2 substantially extends evaluated comparisons: Rex-RK4 versus DDIM with a VAE reconstruction reference in Table 8, native IsoDiff latents versus ConDA embeddings in Table 10, and MLP versus kNN lifting in Table 11. The existing interpolation, PCA/β-VAE, SVM, and CcGAN comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: The additional forecasting experiment specifies 20-frame histories and prediction horizons of 12, 7, and 11 frames for fluid, calcium, and DISFA respectively. New solver experiments compare 8-step Rex-RK4 with 1000-step DDIM. The reported monkey S4 latent dimension changes from 12 to 16, and evaluation adds firing-rate correlation and RMSE dimensionality sweeps. These include new protocols and a revised configuration, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantial checks of inversion error relative to VAE reconstruction, robustness across solvers and diffusion models, and decoder choice through kNN-versus-MLP ablation. Figure 5 adds generated-spike and firing-rate checks, while the dimensionality analysis gains RMSE curves. The earlier orthogonality analysis is retained as Appendix C.7.

E5.justification: Both versions report ± summaries and mean/std-style quantities without explicit random-seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. v2 continues the same reporting practice; additional result rows and changed uncertainty values do not establish a new statistical procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds forecasting and solver/decoder results and revises the dimensionality-sweep curves. Figure 5 replaces the monkey results: ConDA RMSE changes from 1.46 ± 0.45 to 0.67 ± 0.04 under the revised latent configuration, preventing a same-setting improvement comparison; firing-rate correlation r = 0.95 is newly reported. Table 1, the PCA/β-VAE comparison, classification scores, and CcGAN results retain their numerical values.

T1.justification: v2 removes the explicit CcGAN soft-vicinal discriminator and generator loss definitions from v1 Appendix B.1.1. It retains the CcGAN inversion loss and consolidates diffusion equations into algorithms. The central InfoNCE, spline, Taylor, and KDE mathematics remains equivalent, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central claims about separating editing from rendering and obtaining controllable representations across five domains remain. v2 adds explicit claims of robustness across inversion solvers and diffusion backbones in the abstract and conclusion, extending the original DDIM-focused account without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: v2 develops a new interpretation of approximation errors, attributing small reconstruction differences to numerical noise and arguing that lifting, inversion, and VAE errors do not impede prediction. It also interprets kNN's advantage over MLP through neighborhood structure. Section 6 expands the earlier brief limitations into explanations of many-to-one ambiguity, long-range distortion, computational cost, and possible mitigations.

D1.justification: v2 adds solver parameters, MLP architecture and size, forecast histories, block and held-out sample counts, additional runtimes, and a fuller algorithmic pipeline. It also supplies DISFA access instructions and the MC Maze archive identifier and license. These materially expand reproducibility information, although code release and the fluid-data link remain promised rather than supplied.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning against NoiseCLR and DRCT, clarifies the relationship to diffusion/state-space models and LDNS, and introduces a discussion of reversible inversion literature including Rex-RK4, EDICT, BELM, and MALI. Some earlier sequential-diffusion and PIRD references disappear. These substantive changes go beyond publication metadata updates to retained citations.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method exposition, and results narrative are extensively rewritten. Appendix B reorganizes previously separate descriptions into two end-to-end algorithms and adds a DISFA running example; Appendix C is reordered, and an Impact Statement is introduced. This constitutes substantial narrative and structural revision.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column layout. Figure 2 gains a Slerp row, the classification display is separated from Figure 3 into Table 3, Figure 5 gains multiple panels, and the dimensionality plots are redrawn with an RMSE row. New forecasting, solver, and decoder tables and a forecasting figure further expand the displays.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens assessment of the central pipeline through explicit held-out forecasting, solver/VAE reconstruction controls, and a learned-decoder comparison (Tables 2 and 8–11), supported by clearer procedures and implementation details. These address important gaps in v1 concerning generalization and approximation errors. Claims that errors are negligible remain stronger than the controls establish, and some baseline mathematical detail is removed, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains in empirical support and reproducibility.
